Addendum fixed. Combined round commit hashes: 17c5f06, 1f1cb2b, faaf49f (prior rounds, unchanged) plus 3a75dcb (this addendum) on fix/spec-backed-enforcement.

pathAllowed(target, entries, repoRoot) now also resolves target against repoRoot via filepath.Rel — same guard shape as readsContain (preconditions.go, PR #328 precedent): reject a ".."-prefixed Rel result. It tries mission.PathContainedBy against both the raw cleaned target (so the absolute contract-path entry still matches directly) and the repo-relative form (so an ordinary absolute Write/Edit target now matches an ordinary relative write_set entry like docs/**). No new absoluteness-detection branch was needed for the drive-letter case: filepath.Rel already refuses to reconcile absoluteness between a POSIX repoRoot and a drive-letter target by its own OS-native rule, which is exactly "resolves only if the repo root is also drive-lettered" — I added a test proving it resolves when repoRoot itself carries the same drive-letter prefix (TestPathAllowed_DriveLetterTargetNotAdmittedByRelativeEntry, new assertion at the end) and stays refused against a POSIX repoRoot (existing rows, now with a comment explaining why).

repoRoot is threaded from envRepoRoot() at both of HandlePreToolUse's call sites (the write_set-allowlist check and the extract_into stat-then-allow check).

Tests in internal/hook/pretooluse_test.go: TestPathAllowed's /docs/x.md row relabeled "out-of-repo absolute target..." (matches its actual semantics now), new "repo-root-anchored absolute target admitted by relative glob entry" row (true), absolute-match row annotated as unaffected by repo-root resolution since /abs/contract.yaml isn't under the test's fictional /repo root. TestPathAllowed_GlobEntry, TestPathAllowed_GlobDoesNotAdmitTraversal, and the drive-letter test all updated for the new repoRoot parameter and re-verified none of the traversal/escape guarantees regressed.
